summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her fourth cycle of high-dose methotrexate for primary colonic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CNS involvement. She had a history of C. difficile infection from a prior admission and was continuing oral vancomycin. During this stay, her stool tested negative for C. difficile toxin, but she had ongoing high ostomy output, prompting electrolyte repletion and a short course of rifaximin for possible bacterial overgrowth. Methotrexate was administered at a reduced dose of 3500 mg/m², with leucovorin rescue started 24 hours post-infusion. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, and she developed mild mucositis with oral candidiasis, treated with fluconazole and oral care products. Her diabetes was managed with insulin due to persistent hyperglycemia, though she was transitioned back to metformin at discharge. She was discharged home with continued vancomycin, new prescriptions for fluconazole and acyclovir for prophylaxis, and supplements for potassium and magnesium.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Other malignant lymphomas, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
